papers.title: Moral Foundations of Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Probes LLMs for moral foundations using survey instruments, revealing sensitivity to prompt format and systematic biases in how models respond to moral foundations questionnaires.

papers.title: Systematic Bias in LLMs: Discrepant Response Patterns in Binary vs. Continuous Formats
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates systematic discrepancies in LLM responses between binary and continuous response formats, showing that format choice fundamentally alters measured attitudes and values.

papers.title: Decoding LLM Personality Measurement: Forced-Choice Approaches
papers.abstract_snippet: Investigates forced-choice item formats for measuring LLM personality, comparing them to Likert-scale approaches and demonstrating how format choice impacts measurement outcomes.

papers.title: Likert or Not: LLM Absolute Relevance Judgments
papers.abstract_snippet: Examines whether LLMs can reliably produce Likert-scale judgments, finding systematic biases in how models use rating scales compared to human respondents.

papers.title: Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.abstract_snippet: Applies cognitive psychology experimental paradigms to GPT-3, finding format-dependent response patterns that differ systematically from human baselines.

papers.title: Whose Opinions Do Language Models Reflect?
papers.authors: Santurkar, S., Durmus, E., Ladhak, F., Lee, C., Liang, P., & Hashimoto, T.
papers.abstract_snippet: Investigates whose opinions are encoded in language model outputs, showing systematic biases that interact with question format and measurement approach.

papers.title: Out of One, Many: Using Language Models to Simulate Human Samples
papers.abstract_snippet: Demonstrates that LLMs can simulate human survey responses when given demographic personas, but response format and prompt design significantly affect the fidelity of simulation.

papers.title: Established Psychometric vs. Ecologically Valid Questionnaires: Rethinking Assessments in LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Contrasts established psychometric instruments with ecologically valid alternatives for LLM assessment, arguing that standard questionnaires may produce invalid measurements due to format mismatch.

papers.title: Robustness of large language models in moral judgements
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests the robustness of LLM moral judgments under various perturbations including format changes, finding significant sensitivity to presentation format.

papers.title: A Theory-grounded Measure of Political Bias in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_snippet: Develops a theory-grounded approach to measuring political bias in LLMs, demonstrating how measurement format affects detected bias patterns and arguing for format-aware assessment designs.
